title: Stress Testing Hydropower Operation Under Variable Renewable Energy Integration: Potential Impacts and Dynamically Adaptive Strategies
content:
Abstract

Hydropower with reservoir offers a compelling combination of stability and flexibility services for regional socio-economic development and power system. However, its operational paradigm is poorly characterized in the rapidly evolving power system, missing opportunities to effectively balance variable renewable energy (VRE) integration and multisectoral water resource management demand, and failing to address changing values and dynamically adapt to new external environments. With the aim of understanding how dramatic increases in VRE penetrate hydropower operations, we propose an extension of Stochastic Dual Dynamic Programming (SDDP), termed the State Tracking-SDDP (ST-SDDP) framework. This approach identifies the effects of large-scale VRE integration on hydropower operations and derives adaptive operational decision-making strategies. We implement the modeling framework on a hydro-wind-solar clean energy base in Southwest China. Real simulations indicate that ST-SDDP can design the new operational paradigm to capture seasonal variations and address multiple coupled uncertainties related to inflow and VRE output through the effective management of water levels at key periods, including the end of pre-flood and flood seasons. Furthermore, we demonstrate that hydropower operational performance varies with VRE integration capacity, and hydropower would take on increased operational risks to enhance overall system efficiency, with the balance of these risks closely tied to VRE integration capacity and transmission channel capacity.
